registry.description: Rejection is the experience of being turned away — refused, excluded, deemed unworthy or unwanted by someone whose acceptance mattered. The Greek term here (aposterēsis) covers the deprivation of what one was owed or expected. Rejection in Scripture is both an experience Jesus himself undergoes (he was despised and rejected) and a dynamic at the heart of the human-God relationship: the story of Israel and of humanity is in part the story of rejecting the One who comes to them. The one rejected by humans is vindicated by God.
registry.inference_note: Rejection as a psychological inner state — the felt experience of being unwanted or cast away — is ABSENT as a single biblical term. Scripture addresses rejection primarily from the perspective of being rejected by God or by people, with some texts addressing the inner experience.
